Employee Creation

Purpose

This guide explains how to create an Employee record in the system and the minimum information required to make the employee usable for HR operations (leave, payroll, attendance, approvals, and reporting).

Who Can Create Employees

Only users with the correct HR permissions should create Employee records, typically: - HR Manager - HR User (with create/write rights on Employee) - System Manager (for setup and support)

Preconditions

Before creating an employee, confirm the following records already exist: - Company - Department - Designation - Branch (if used) - Reports To manager (if known) - Employment Type / Contract Type (if configured) - User account (if the employee needs system login)

Navigation

  1. Open Home.

  2. Search for Employee.

  3. Click New.

Employee Creation Steps

  1. In the Employee form, complete identity fields:

  • First Name

  • Middle Name (optional)

  • Last Name

  • Gender

  • Date of Birth

  1. Complete employment details:

  • Company

  • Employee Number (if manual numbering is enabled)

  • Date of Joining

  • Department

  • Designation

  • Employment Type

  • Status (set to Active for current staff)

  1. Complete organization and reporting details:

  • Branch (if applicable)

  • Reports To

  • Grade (if applicable)

  1. Complete contact details:

  • Prefered Email / Company Email

  • Personal Email (optional)

  • Cell Number

  1. Complete payroll and HR control fields where applicable:

  • Holiday List

  • Default Shift

  • Leave Approver

  • Expense Approver

  • Attendance Device ID (if biometric integration exists)

  1. If the employee requires portal/system access:

  • Link a User ID

  • Ensure role assignment is handled by HR/IT policy

  1. Click Save.

Recommended Post-Creation Actions

After saving the employee record: 1. Create or verify user account and role profile. 2. Create employment contract (if your process requires it). 3. Assign leave policy / leave allocation. 4. Confirm payroll inclusion and salary structure assignment. 5. Confirm reporting line and approvers.

Validation Checklist

Use this checklist before considering setup complete: - Employee status is Active. - Department and designation are correct. - Date of joining is correct. - Employee is linked to the correct company. - Approvers are set (leave/expense where required). - Contact and email details are valid. - User ID is linked (if login is required).

Common Errors and Fixes

  • Missing mandatory fields: Complete highlighted mandatory fields then save again.

  • Invalid company/department/designation: Create the missing master records first.

  • No naming series/employee number issue: Confirm Employee naming settings and series permissions.

  • Approver not selectable: Ensure the approver employee/user is active and has required permissions.

  • User link not allowed: Verify the email/user exists and is not linked to another employee incorrectly.

Data Quality Rules

  • Use official names exactly as in legal/HR documents.

  • Use company email as primary where policy requires.

  • Do not duplicate employee records for the same person.

  • Keep status updated (Active, Left, Suspended) for accurate reporting.

Audit and Control

  • Employee creation should follow HR onboarding approval.

  • Changes to key fields (department, designation, reports to, status) should be traceable.

  • Periodically review active employee list for data accuracy.

Related Documents

  • Employee Onboarding Process

  • Contract Management Guide

  • Leave Allocation Guide

  • Payroll Setup Guide

Performance Appraisals

Purpose

This guide explains how HR runs performance appraisals end to end: building a reusable template, creating an appraisal cycle for many staff at once, the supervisor review and automatic grading, and how progress and results appear on the HR Management dashboard.

Key Concepts

  • Performance Appraisal Template - the reusable definition of an appraisal: performance areas & criteria, the rating scale, score bands, and the supervisor-comment questions. One template is marked Active and is used by default.
  • Performance Appraisal Cycle - an HR batch covering one evaluation period. HR selects employees once and submits; the system creates one appraisal per employee.
  • Performance Appraisal - the individual record completed by a supervisor for one employee.

1. Set up a template (once)

Go to Performance Appraisal Template and create a new record. On a new template the following are prefilled with sensible defaults that you can edit:

  • Performance Areas - each area with its criteria (e.g. Job Knowledge and Skills, Quality of Work).
  • Rating Scale - pulled from the Performance Appraisal Rating scale reference (1-5 descriptions).
  • Score Bands - the percentage bands that turn a score into a rating (Exceptional, Strong Performer, … Unacceptable) and the recommended action for each.
  • Supervisor Comments - the open-ended questions the supervisor answers (Highlights, Development Needs, etc.).

Tick Active and save. Only one template can be active at a time; activating a new one deactivates the previous. Update questions here at any time - future appraisals pick up the change.

2. Create an appraisal cycle

From the HR Management dashboard open the Performance Appraisal tab and click + New Appraisal Cycle (or create a Performance Appraisal Cycle directly). Set:

  • Evaluation Type and the From / To dates of the period.
  • Appraisal Template - leave blank to use the active template.
  • Employees - add every staff member who should be appraised this cycle.

3. Submit the cycle

Submitting the cycle creates one Performance Appraisal per employee, seeded from the template, and emails each employee’s supervisor (the employee is CC’d) asking them to complete it. Employees with no supervisor (reports_to) are skipped and flagged on the cycle. You can do this for many employees in a single action.

4. Supervisor completes the appraisal

The supervisor opens the appraisal, rates each performance area, answers the comment questions, and submits it back to HR. Email notifications are sent on every workflow transition (to supervisor, to HR, on approval, rejection, or request for clarification).

5. Automatic grading

When the supervisor submits to HR, the appraisal is graded automatically:

  • Total = sum of the area ratings (max 5 per area).
  • Score (%) = total ÷ (number of areas × 5).
  • Performance Rating = the highest score band the percentage meets, with its Recommended Action.

These fields appear in the Performance Score section of the appraisal. Because the maximum scales with the number of performance areas, grading stays correct even if the template changes.

6. HR review

HR approves, rejects, or requests clarification. A cycle is Completed only when every appraisal in it reaches Approved by HR; otherwise it shows as In Progress.

Dashboard

The Performance Appraisal tab on the HR Management dashboard shows:

  • A toggle to list only incomplete cycles, with per-cycle Total / Completed / Pending counts and status.
  • Charts of graded appraisals: Performance Rating Distribution and Average Score by Department, plus headline metrics.

Roles

  • HR Manager creates templates and cycles, submits cycles, and approves/rejects appraisals.
  • Supervisor completes and submits the appraisals for their direct reports.

Jira Integration

Purpose

This guide explains how to connect the system to Jira Cloud, sync Jira projects and their issues (tasks), and link those issues to ERPNext Tasks so project work stays in one place.

Key Concepts

  • Jira Settings - a single settings record holding the Jira connection (site URL, account email, API token).

  • Jira Project - a copy of a Jira project pulled into the system. Each one carries a child table of its issues/tasks.

  • Jira Issue - a row under a Jira Project mirroring a Jira issue (key, summary, type, status, assignee, dates, sprint, etc.).

  • Jira Sprint - a record for each distinct Jira sprint seen on pulled issues (name, state, board, start/end date, goal), linked back to its Jira Project.

  • ERPNext Task - the native task record. Jira issues are linked to Tasks with Task Source = Jira.

1. Connect to Jira (once)

Open Jira Settings and enter:

  • Site URL - e.g. https://yourcompany.atlassian.net (must start with https://).

  • Account Email - the Atlassian account email.

  • API Token - created at id.atlassian.com > Security > API tokens.

Save, then click Test Connection. A green message confirms the credentials.

Note on the API Token: it is a password field and shows masked dots after saving. Leave it untouched on later edits - saving the form will keep the stored token. Only type into it when you genuinely want to replace the token.

2. Pull Jira projects

In Jira Settings use:

  • Pull Projects - imports/updates all Jira projects you can access into Jira Project records.

  • Pull Project by Key - previews a single project (e.g. ER) without saving.

3. Pull issues (tasks) for a project

Open a Jira Project and click Pull Issues from Jira. The system fetches every issue in that project and rebuilds the Tasks / Issues table from scratch, so Jira remains the source of truth and re-syncing never creates duplicates or conflicts.

Each issue row stores: Issue Key, Summary, Type, Status, Priority, Assignee, Reporter, Parent Key, Labels, Resolution, Created, Updated, Start Date, Due Date, Sprint, and a direct URL to the issue.

Start Date and Sprint are read from Jira's own Start date and Sprint fields. These are matched by field name automatically on every pull (Jira exposes them as custom fields with a site-specific ID under the hood, so nothing needs to be configured) - if an issue has neither set, its Start Date / Sprint are simply left blank.

4. Link issues to ERPNext Tasks

To create native Tasks from Jira issues, link the Jira project to an ERPNext Project first:

  1. Open the relevant Project and set the Jira Project field to the matching Jira project (e.g. ER).

  2. On the Jira Project, click Pull Issues from Jira.

For every issue, an ERPNext Task is created or updated under that project, with:

  • Task Source = Jira, and the Jira Issue Key / Jira Issue URL recorded for traceability.

  • Subject from the issue summary, Expected Start Date from Jira's Start date, Expected End Date from the due date.

  • Status mapped from Jira (Done/Closed/Resolved → Completed, In Progress → Working, In Review → Pending Review, otherwise Open).

  • Priority mapped from Jira (Highest → Urgent, High → High, Medium → Medium, Low/Lowest → Low).

  • Allocate To - the Jira assignee's email is matched against each Employee's User ID. If an Employee is found, the Task's Allocate To field is set to that Employee. If no match is found (the assignee isn't an Employee on the ERP), the raw email is kept on the Task's Jira Assignee Email field instead so the information isn't lost.

  • Jira Sprint - set to the matching Jira Sprint record when the issue belongs to one.

Tasks are matched on the Jira Issue Key, so repeated pulls update the same Task rather than duplicating it. Issues with no linked ERPNext Project are still stored on the Jira Project, but no Task is created until a Project is linked.

5. Sprints

Every distinct sprint seen while pulling issues is upserted into a Jira Sprint record (name, state, board, start/end date, goal), linked to its Jira Project. You don't pull sprints separately - they're derived automatically from each issue's Sprint field during Pull Issues from Jira.

To see a project's sprints, open its Jira Project record and use the Jira Sprint entry in the sidebar connections. Tasks synced from Jira carry a Jira Sprint link field, so Tasks can be filtered/grouped by sprint to organise work coming from Jira.

Sync behaviour & conflicts

  • The Jira Project issues table is fully rebuilt on each pull - it always reflects current Jira state.

  • ERPNext Tasks are upserted by Issue Key - safe to re-run anytime.

  • The flow is currently one-way (Jira → ERPNext). Changes made in ERPNext are not pushed back to Jira.

Troubleshooting

  • 410 Gone on pull: Jira removed older search endpoints; the integration uses the current /rest/api/3/search/jql endpoint.

  • Connection fails: re-check the Site URL (https), email, and regenerate the API token.

  • No Tasks created: confirm the ERPNext Project has its Jira Project field set.

  • Start Date or Sprint always blank: the lookup matches Jira's field by its exact display name (Start date / Sprint). If your Jira instance uses a different label for these fields, or the fields simply aren't enabled on the issue's screen, they won't be found.

  • Allocate To not set: the Jira assignee's email must exactly match an Employee's User ID on the ERP. Otherwise the email is stored on Jira Assignee Email instead.

Purpose

This guide explains how to record project meeting minutes in the system using the Project Meeting Minutes document, so that attendance, discussions, action points and next-meeting plans are captured in one place and linked to the project.

Key Concepts

  • Project Meeting Minutes - the main record for a single meeting. It is submittable, so once finalised it can be submitted to lock the content.

  • Attendees - a table listing each person present or absent, with their department/company and attendance status.

  • Agenda - a table of agenda items, each with discussion summaries, action points, RACI and timelines.

1. Create the Minutes

There are two ways to start:

  • Open the Project, click the Create action dropdown and choose Meeting Minutes. The project is filled in automatically.

  • Or go to the Project Meeting Minutes list and click New, then pick the project.


2. Meeting Details

  • Meeting Title - a clear name, e.g. Project Y Demo Meeting.

  • Date - the meeting date (defaults to today).

  • Location - the venue, or Virtual for online meetings.

  • Call Recording - paste the recording link if there is one.

3. Attendees

Add a row per person. Set Status to In Attendance for those present, or Absent with Apology for those who sent apologies. Record their Department/Company.

4. Agenda Details

Add a row per agenda item:

  • Agenda - a short label of the issue discussed.

  • Summaries from Discussion - the important points raised.

  • Action Points - what needs to be done.

  • RACI - who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed.

  • Timelines - the due dates or timeframes.

5. Next Meeting

Record the Date of the next meeting and its Objective.

6. Save and Submit

Click Save to keep a draft you can keep editing. When the minutes are final, click Submit to lock them. Submitted minutes can still be amended if a correction is needed.

Where to Find Them

All minutes for a project are listed under the project's Connections tab, in the Reports group as Project Meeting Minutes, or Under ICL Project Management dashbord.

Purpose

A Lessons Learned Report captures the experience of a project so the team can repeat what worked and avoid what did not. The questions are driven by the active Lessons Learned Template (managed by HR/System Admin), so they stay consistent across all projects.

When to Capture Lessons

  • At project closure, or after a major milestone, phase, or significant incident.

  • When the team wants to capture what worked, what did not, and what to repeat or avoid next time.

  • Before handover, so knowledge stays with the organization and not just individuals.

How to Complete the Report


  1. From the project, click Start Lessons Learned Report - the project title and client are pre-filled for you.

  2. Answer the narrative questions. These come from the active Lessons Learned Template and may change over time.

  3. Fill the Root Cause Analysis table: list each issue, its underlying root cause, and the area affected.

  4. Add Recommendations with a priority (High/Medium/Low) so improvements can be ranked.

  5. Define Next Steps as concrete action items with a responsible person, deadline, and status.

  6. Attach supporting documentation, then route to the supervisor for sign-off and submit.

Browsing Reports

The Lessons Learned tab in the ICL Project Management sidebar lists every report regardless of status (Draft, Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Needs Clarification), with the project, reporter and status shown at a glance. Use New Lessons Learned Report there to start one, or click a report to open it. This is separate from the Knowledge Base below, which only lists Approved reports.

Exporting the Branded Report

Once a report is Approved, open it from the Knowledge Base tab of ICL Project Management and click Export .docx. This generates an IntelliSOFT-branded Word document (letterhead, project info table, narrative, root cause / recommendations / next steps tables, and footer) ready to share or archive.

Lessons Learned Knowledge Base

Every Approved report is automatically indexed in the company-wide Knowledge Base, found under the Knowledge Base tab of ICL Project Management. Any IntelliSOFT staff member can search it by:

  • Keyword - matches issues, root causes, recommendations, and action items.

  • Project Type - e.g. Internal, Client, Research.

  • Area - Technical, Process, Communication, Resource, Risk, Other.

  • Recommendation Priority - High, Medium, Low.

Each result can be expanded to view its root causes, recommendations and next steps, or exported straight to .docx.

Surfaced During Project Setup

When a new Project's Project Type is set, the Project form shows an alert and a View Related Lessons Learned button if approved reports exist for that project type - helping new PMs learn from similar past projects before they start.

High Level Work Plan

Purpose

The High Level Work Plan (HLWP) captures the major line items and key deliverables of a project on a single timeline. It gives the team and stakeholders a top-down view of what will be delivered, when, by whom, and the current status - without the task-level detail.

Key Concepts

  • Project - each HLWP is linked to one Project. The project's Work Plan tab reads from this link.
  • Project Lead, Start/End Date, Duration - header fields summarising ownership and timeline.
  • Work Plan Items - the table of line items, each with a key deliverable, dates, expected outcome, status, resources and comments.
  • Key Deliverable - a linked Project Key Deliverable; new values are created automatically on import.
  • Entry Type - either System Entry (filled in directly) or Template Import (uploaded from an Excel template).

1. Create a High Level Work Plan

Open New → High Level Work Plan and set the Project, Project Lead and the start/end dates. The naming series is HLW-.YYYY.-.MM.-.

2a. System Entry

Set Entry Type = System Entry and add rows to the High Level Workplan Table. For each item provide:

  • Line Item - the activity or work package name.
  • Key Deliverable - the output it produces.
  • Start Date / End Date - the planned window.
  • Expected Outcome - what success looks like.
  • Status - NOT STARTED, IN PROGRESS, or COMPLETED.
  • Resources and Comments - supporting notes.

2b. Template Import

Set Entry Type = Template Import and attach the completed Excel file under Template Import. On save, the rows are read from the spreadsheet and loaded into the table. The importer scans the first rows to detect the header line (line_item, key_deliverable, start_date, end_date, expected_outcome, status, resources, comments), so the column order is flexible. Download the blank template from the project's Work Plan tab using Download Template.

3. View on the Project Dashboard

Open the project in ICL Project Management and go to the Work Plan tab. The High Level Work Plan shows a summary strip (Lead, dates, duration, item count, % completed), an overall completion bar, and the searchable, filterable items table. Use Open Plan to edit the underlying document.

Detailed Work Plan

Purpose

The Detailed Work Plan (DWP) breaks a project down to the activity level. Where the High Level Work Plan shows major line items, the DWP lists the individual activities, their level of effort, and the resources assigned, giving the delivery team an executable plan.

Key Concepts

  • Project - each DWP links to one Project and appears on its Work Plan tab.
  • Client - the linked Customer the work is delivered for.
  • Developer / IntelliSOFT Project Lead - the people responsible for delivery.
  • Project Timeline, Start Date, End Date - the overall schedule.
  • Detailed Workplan Items - the activity table.

1. Create a Detailed Work Plan

Open New → Detailed Work Plan, link the Project and Client, and record the developer, lead and timeline. The naming series is DWP-.YYYY.-.MM.-.

2. Add Activities

In the Detailed workplan table add a row per activity with:

  • Item - the activity reference or grouping.
  • Activities - the work to be done.
  • Expected Outcomes & Deliverables - what the activity produces.
  • Resources - who or what is required.
  • Start Date / End Date - the activity window.
  • Duration LOE - level of effort, in days.
  • Status - the current progress of the activity.

3. Google Drive Link

If the plan is maintained as a spreadsheet, paste its shared link in Google Drive link so the team can reach the source document from the record.

4. View on the Project Dashboard

On the project's Work Plan tab, the Detailed Work Plan appears below the High Level plan. Use Open Plan to edit the activities.

Project Risk Assessment

Purpose

The Project Risk Assessment records the risks facing a project, rates each one for severity and likelihood, and captures the recommended mitigation, giving the team a single place to track and review project risk.

Key Concepts

  • Project - the assessment links to one Project; Client, Project Start Date and Project End Date are fetched from it automatically.
  • Developer / IntelliSOFT Project Director - the people accountable for the assessment.
  • Risk Assessment List - the table of individual risks.
  • Risk Assessment Matrix - the Likelihood × Severity grid used to rate each risk.

1. Create a Risk Assessment

Open New → Project Risk Assessment, link the Project (Client and dates fill in automatically) and record the Developer and IntelliSOFT Project Director.

2. Add Risks

On the Risk Assessment List tab, add a row per risk with:

  • Risk - a short description of the risk.
  • Areas Affected - the part(s) of the project it threatens.
  • Severity and Likelihood - rate using the Risk Assessment Matrix below.
  • Risk Impact - the resulting rating (Low / Medium / High).
  • Recommended Action(s) - the mitigation or response plan.

3. Risk Assessment Matrix

Use the matrix to convert a risk's Likelihood and Severity into its overall Risk Impact rating:

Purpose

Project Management Settings is the single, module-wide configuration record for the Project Management area. It holds the current roster of Project Managers and the contacts used by automated project notifications, so they don't need to be hard-coded per project.

Where to Find It

Open ICL Project Management, then use the page menu (⋮) and select Project Management Settings. It can also be opened directly via New → Project Management Settings or the Awesomebar, since it is a single (one record per site).


Project Managers Tab

  • Lead Project Manager - the User who heads the Project Management function. Required.

  • Project Managers - the table of all active Project Managers. Each row links an Employee (Employee Name and Department are fetched automatically) and tracks whether their Email Sent welcome notification has gone out. Keep this list current so PM-wide communications and workload views reflect who is actively managing projects.

Automation Tab

  • Finance Escalation Contact - a User notified alongside the assigned Project Manager(s) when a project's Sales Invoice becomes 7+ days overdue. Invoices overdue by 45+ days additionally escalate to users with the CEO role. Leave blank to skip this extra recipient.

Who Can Access It

Full access (create, read, write, delete, share) is limited to the System Manager, PM Lead, Finance, and Projects Manager roles.

Purpose

The Project Toolkit Document Templates list is the single library of standard templates used across every project - project charters, work plans, status report formats, risk assessment matrices, lessons learned templates and more. Maintain a template once here and it stays available for every project, instead of PMs hunting for the latest version or emailing files around.

Where to Find It

Search Project Toolkit Document Templates in the Awesomebar, or go to New -> Project Toolkit Document Templates to add one. As a Project Manager you have full create and edit access to this list.


Key Fields

  • Document Name - a clear, unique label for the template (e.g. "Project charter template"). This also becomes the record's ID.

  • Attach - upload the actual template file (Word, Excel, PDF, etc.).

  • Description - a short note on what the template is for and when to use it.

  • Is Active - tick once the template is ready to use. Inactive templates are skipped everywhere they would otherwise be used.

  • Project Phase (Availability) - the table of project phases and folders this template should be copied into. For each row, set the Project Phase and target Folder, and tick Available to enable that placement.

How to Add or Update a Template

  1. Open New -> Project Toolkit Document Templates (or open the existing record if you are replacing a file).

  2. Set the Document Name and Description.

  3. Attach the file under Attach.

  4. In Project Phase (Availability), add a row for each phase/folder combination where this template should appear, ticking Available for each.

  5. Tick Is Active and save.

To roll out a newer version of an existing template, simply replace the file under Attach on that same record and save - there is no need to create a new record or touch individual projects.

How Templates Reach a Project

Being active is not enough on its own - a template also needs to be selected in HIS Project Lifecycle Config (a System Manager / PM Lead setting) under Project Toolkit Document Templates and Project Toolkit Folders. Once selected there, opening a project and clicking Create Drive Folder builds the full phase/folder structure in Google Drive and copies every configured, active template into its assigned folder(s) automatically.

If a template you added is not showing up in new project folders, ask your PM Lead or System Admin to check that it is selected in HIS Project Lifecycle Config.

  • Project Module - creating a project and generating its Google Drive folder.

Project Notifications & Automation

Purpose

A set of scheduled jobs keeps Project Managers, Finance and the CEO informed automatically - status reports, milestones, invoices and project closeout - without anyone having to chase updates manually.

1. Status Report Reminder

Trigger: a daily check, evaluated against each project's own Project Report Frequency.

One day before a status report is due, the assigned Project Manager(s) get both an email and an in-app notification with a direct link to create the report.

2. Weekly PM Digest

Trigger: every Monday at 7:00am.

Each PM receives one personalised email covering their assigned projects: active projects and status, milestones due in the next 7 days, overdue tasks, open High impact risk items, and recent meeting action points from the last 7 days (the project's communication log).

3. Milestone Approaching Alert

Trigger: a daily check.

The Project Manager is notified 3 days and again 1 day before a milestone task's due date. If a milestone passes its due date without being marked Completed, the PM is notified again every 2 days until it is resolved.

4. Overdue Invoice Escalation

Trigger: every Monday at 8:00am.

For unpaid Sales Invoices linked to a project:

  • 7+ days overdue - notify the Project Manager(s), users with the Finance role, and the Finance Escalation Contact configured in Project Management Settings.
  • 45+ days overdue - additionally notify users with the CEO role. The PM can update the project's expected payment dates directly on the Project's Project Payment Schedule table if the timeline has changed.

5. Project Closure Checklist

Trigger: when a Project's Project Phase changes to Post-Implementation Closeout.

Three Tasks are generated automatically for the Project Manager, each due 7 days out: Upload lessons learned, Confirm all invoices paid, and Archive project documents.

  • HIS Project Quick Guide - the overall project lifecycle checklist.
  • Lessons Learned - completing the closeout report referenced above.

Timesheet Submission

Purpose

The Timesheet Submission is an employee's monthly record of hours worked across projects. It is the document that moves through the approval workflow - from the employee, through review, to Finance - and on final approval the underlying Timesheet records are confirmed in the system.

Key Concepts

  • Timesheet Submission - one per employee per month (naming series TS-). It is submittable, so it locks once Finance approves.
  • Timesheet Template - either Default (regular staff) or Short Term Consultant. This is derived from the employee's Contract Type and decides which approval path the submission follows.
  • Timesheet Per Project - the table listing hours against each project for the month.
  • Total Working Hours - the sum that must be greater than zero before submission.
  • Finance Breakdown - on Finance review, salary (CTC), salary per hour and total billable hours are computed for costing.

1. Create the Submission

  1. Go to New → Timesheet Submission.
  2. Select the Employee - the name and Timesheet Template are derived automatically.
  3. Set the Month-Year the submission covers.

2. Enter Hours and Generate Timesheets

Add the project lines under Timesheet Per Project and generate the underlying Timesheet entries in the system. The workflow enforces two gates before the submission can leave Draft:

  • Total Working Hours must be greater than 0.
  • Timesheet entries must already be inserted for the submission (a generated Timesheet linked to it).

If either is missing, submission is blocked with a message.

3. The Approval Workflow

The path depends on the employee's Timesheet Template. Rejections and clarification requests always return the document to Draft so the employee can correct and resubmit.

Regular Staff (Default template)

Draft → Submitted to Supervisor → Submitted to Finance → Approved by Finance

Short Term Consultant

Draft → Submitted to Project Manager → Submitted to Supervisor → Submitted to Finance → Approved by Finance

Short Term Consultants have an extra Project Manager review first, because their time is billed to specific projects.

Reviewing & Requesting Clarification

Reviewers do more than approve. At each review stage - Project Manager, Supervisor and Finance - the reviewer can open and examine the submitted timesheet entries and, instead of approving, choose Request for Clarification. This returns the submission to Draft, records the reviewer's note as a comment on the document, and emails the employee the clarification message so they can correct and resubmit.

4. Finance Approval & Outcome

When Finance approves, the submission reaches Approved by Finance and is submitted (locked). At this point the system finalises the linked Timesheet records and computes the finance breakdown (employee CTC, salary per hour and total billable hours) used for project costing.

From an approved submission, Finance can download the timesheet report (Project Ratios) - an Excel export listing the hours per project and each project's ratio (%) of the total (used for QuickBooks billing), followed by a per-project task matrix of the inserted timesheet entries.

5. Reminders & Notifications

Each transition notifies the next approver. Employees who have not submitted for the period can be chased through the non-submitter reminder. Clarification requests carry the reviewer's note back to the employee.

Supervisor SLA Reminder & Nudge

While a submission sits in Submitted to Supervisor, the system tracks how long it has been waiting and can act once a configured SLA is breached:

  • Employee overdue notice - once the SLA is breached, the employee is emailed (and gets an in-app notification) that their submission has not yet been reviewed.
  • Nudge Supervisor - while still pending, the employee can click Nudge Supervisor on the Timesheet Submission form to send the supervisor an immediate reminder email. This is rate-limited by a configurable cooldown so the supervisor isn't repeatedly pinged.
  • Auto-remind Supervisor - optionally, the system can remind the supervisor automatically on SLA breach, without the employee needing to nudge.

These rules are configured per doctype under HR Config → Reminder Rules (SLA hours, plus toggles for the employee notice, auto-reminder, and nudge/cooldown). The same mechanism can be extended to other approval workflows beyond Timesheet Submission.

Employee Annual Leave Balance

Purpose

Every Employee record has a Leave Balance section showing, at a glance, how many days of each leave type are allocated, used and remaining for the current period - without needing to open Leave Allocation or Leave Application records separately.

Where to Find It

Open the employee's Employee record and go to the Leave Balance section. It refreshes automatically every time the form loads.

What It Shows

The Leave Balance Summary table lists one row per Leave Type the employee currently has an active allocation for (today falls within the allocation's From Date / To Date), with:

  • Allocated - total leave days allocated for the period.
  • Used - days taken from approved, submitted Leave Applications that fall within the allocation period.
  • Balance - Allocated minus Used.
  • From Date / To Date - the allocation period.

The table is read-only and rebuilt each time the form is opened - it is not saved data on the Employee record itself.

Raising a Balance Issue

If the numbers look wrong (e.g. a leave was not deducted, or an allocation is missing), click Raise Leave Balance Issue below the summary table, describe the problem, and click Send to HR. This emails the HR team with the employee's details, the reporter, and the issue description so they can investigate.

Leave Allocation

Purpose

A Leave Allocation is the record that grants an employee a number of days for a specific Leave Type over a period (typically a calendar year). Leave Application requests are checked and deducted against the matching allocation, and the Employee Annual Leave Balance summary is calculated from it.

Automatic Monthly Accrual

Rather than being created by hand for every employee, annual leave is allocated and topped up automatically by a scheduled process, configured in the single Leave Allocation Setting record:

  • Leave Type - the leave type to allocate (e.g. Annual Leave).
  • Days To Add - the number of days accrued per month.
  • Enabled - turns the automated process on or off.
  • HR Email - who receives the run summary/report and any error notifications.

Who Is Eligible

Only active employees whose Contract Type has Accumulate monthly leave checked are included in the run.

How the Monthly Run Works

The process runs automatically on Frappe's monthly schedule:

  1. January (new calendar year): if no allocation exists yet for the configured leave type covering 1 Jan - 31 Dec of the new year, a fresh Leave Allocation is created and submitted for every eligible employee, with Days To Add as the opening balance.
  2. Every other month (or January once the year's allocation exists): each eligible employee's existing annual allocation has its New Leaves Allocated and Total Leaves Allocated increased by Days To Add. An employee already topped up for that calendar month is skipped, so the job can safely run more than once without double-accruing.

After every run, HR receives an email at HR Email summarising how many allocations were created, updated, skipped or failed, with a CSV report attached listing the outcome per employee. Errors during the run are emailed to the same address.

Travel Request Reconciliation

Purpose

The Travel Request Reconciliation accounts for what was actually spent against an approved Travel Request advance. It records the real costs, compares them to the advance, and produces a balance (refund due or top-up). It links back to its Travel Request and runs through a Finance approval workflow.

Key Concepts

  • Travel Request - the approved request being reconciled. The currency, advance and traveller are pulled from it.
  • Total Advance - the amount that was approved on the Travel Request.
  • Actual Allocated Amount - used only when the amount actually disbursed differs from the request. Tick Allocated Amount Differs to reveal and use it; otherwise the Total Advance is used.
  • Activity Participants Reconciliation - the line items of actual spend, each with the amount paid and an FX rate that yields the local-currency amount.
  • Total Spent / Total Balance - computed totals in the Travel Request's currency; the balance is allocated amount minus total spent. Total Local Amount shows the local-currency equivalent.

1. Create the Reconciliation

  1. Go to New → Travel Request Reconciliation and select the Travel Request; the traveller, currency and advance are fetched.
  2. Record the dates (advance taken, reconciliation, trip dates) and project budget code(s).
  3. Add the actual spend rows under Activity Participants Reconciliation (amount paid and FX rate). Totals and balance are calculated automatically.
  4. If the disbursed amount differed from the request, tick Allocated Amount Differs and enter the Actual Allocated Amount.

Email Notifications

The system sends an automatic email on every workflow transition. Notifications are triggered by the on_update hook in the Project Management Lessons Learned controller and use the employee's Company Email (falling back to Personal Email) for delivery.

1. Reporter submits → Supervisor is notified

  • Trigger: State changes from Draft to Submitted to Supervisor.

  • Recipient: The employee's supervisor (the employee linked in the Reports To field of the reporter's Employee record).

  • Subject: Lessons Learned Report <name> submitted for review

  • Content: Supervisor's name, reporter's name, report ID, project name, and a direct link to open the record.

2. Reporter resubmits → Supervisor is notified

  • Trigger: State changes from Needs Clarification to Submitted to Supervisor.

  • Recipient: Same supervisor as above.

  • Subject: Lessons Learned Report <name> resubmitted for review

  • Content: Same as the initial submission email but states the report has been resubmitted.

3. Supervisor approves → Reporter is notified

  • Trigger: State changes to Approved.

  • Recipient: The reporter (employee on the report).

  • Subject: Lessons Learned Report <name> - Approved

  • Content: Congratulatory message with report ID, project name, and a link to view the approved record.

4. Supervisor rejects → Reporter is notified

  • Trigger: State changes to Rejected.

  • Recipient: The reporter.

  • Subject: Lessons Learned Report <name> - Rejected

  • Content: Informs the reporter the report was rejected and asks them to contact their supervisor for guidance.

5. Supervisor requests clarification → Reporter is notified

  • Trigger: State changes to Needs Clarification.

  • Recipient: The reporter.

  • Subject: Lessons Learned Report <name> - Needs Clarification

  • Content: Informs the reporter that the report requires clarification and asks them to address the feedback and resubmit.

Troubleshooting

  • Supervisor did not receive the submission email: Check that the reporter's Employee record has a Reports To value and that the supervisor's Employee record has a valid email. Also check the system's Email Queue (Email Queue list in Frappe) for delivery errors.

  • Reporter did not receive the approval/rejection email: Check the reporter's Employee record for a company or personal email address.

  • Email Queue has errors: Verify the outbound email settings in Email Account (SMTP configuration).

Employee KPI Creation

Purpose

This guide explains how to create an Employee KPI record in the system. KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) define WHAT an employee is expected to deliver during a contract or review period. They form the basis for monthly reflections and quarterly appraisals.

Who Can Create Employee KPIs

  • HR Manager
  • Supervisor (for their direct reports)
  • System Manager (for setup and support)

Preconditions

Before creating an Employee KPI, confirm the following exist:

  • An active Employee record in the system
  • The employee's contract or Job Description is available for reference
  • KPI Categories are configured (if used)
  • The review period / contract period is known

Navigation

  1. Open the ICL Staff workspace.
  2. Under Performance & Development, click Employee KPI.
  3. Click New.

Section A - Employee Information

Complete the header fields that identify the employee and the review period:

  • Employee - select the employee from the list
  • Employee Name - auto-filled from the employee record
  • Job Title - the employee's current job title
  • Department - the employee's department
  • Supervisor - the name of the direct supervisor
  • Review Period - the date marking the start of the review/contract period
  • Contract Type - select the applicable contract type (e.g. Full-time, Consultancy)

Section B - KPI Details Table

Add one row per KPI. Each row captures:

  • KPI# - sequential number for reference (e.g. 1, 2, 3)
  • Strategic Objective - the organisational or departmental goal this KPI supports
  • KPI Category - the category this KPI falls under
  • KPI Description - a clear statement of what the employee must deliver
  • Measure - how performance will be assessed (e.g. % completion, number of reports, rating)
  • Target - the specific result that constitutes success
  • Weight (%) - the relative importance of this KPI; all weights must total 100%
  • Data Source - where evidence of performance will come from (e.g. system report, client feedback)

How to Draft KPIs from a Contract or Job Description

  1. Read the employee's contract and Job Description. Highlight key responsibilities and expected outputs.
  2. Group similar responsibilities into 4-8 main result areas (e.g. project delivery, documentation, client communication, reporting).
  3. For each result area, write one clear KPI that describes the expected result, not just the activity.
  4. For each KPI, define the Measure, Target, and Weight (%).
  5. Ensure all weights add up to 100%. Assign higher weight to more critical areas.

KPI Quality Checklist (SMART)

Each KPI must be:

  • Specific - clearly states what should be achieved
  • Measurable - includes a number, percentage, rating, or deadline that can be verified
  • Achievable - realistic given the time frame and available resources
  • Relevant - linked to the role, department, and organisational goals
  • Time-bound - has a clear period (monthly, quarterly, annual, or contract period)

Saving the Record

  1. Review all rows in the KPI table and confirm weights total 100%.
  2. Click Save.
  3. Share the saved KPI record with the employee for acknowledgement before the review period begins.

Starting a KPI Cycle (Bulk)

To create draft KPIs for many employees at once instead of one at a time:

  1. Open the Employee KPI list view.
  2. Click Start KPI Cycle (visible only to HR Manager and System Manager).
  3. Set the Review Period (required).
  4. Optionally filter by Department and/or Contract Type, or pick specific Employees (this overrides the filters above).
  5. Click Start.

This creates a Draft Employee KPI for every matching Active employee who doesn't already have one for that Review Period. Employees who already have one are skipped and listed in the confirmation message. Each new draft still needs its KPI Details table (Section B) filled in.

Link to Performance Reviews

  • The KPI record is the reference document for the employee's Monthly Reflection.
  • At the end of each quarter, the supervisor uses the same KPIs when completing the Appraisal.
  • Do not change KPIs mid-period unless there is a formal role change or contract amendment.

Common Errors and Fixes

  • Employee not selectable - confirm the Employee record exists and is Active.
  • Weights do not total 100% - adjust individual KPI weights before saving.
  • KPI Category not found - create the required category in the master list first.
  • Blank Measure or Target - every KPI must have both a Measure and a Target to be useful for appraisal.

Purpose

The Grievance form allows an employee to formally raise a workplace concern or complaint by name. All grievances are routed to the Head of Corporate Services and follow a resolution workflow. Employees who prefer not to identify themselves can use the fully anonymous channel instead - see Anonymous Employee Grievance.

Navigation

Form Fields

  • Grievance Against Party - whether it is against an individual, team, or policy
  • Grievance Against - the specific person or entity involved
  • Description - full description of the issue including dates, events, and any witnesses
  • Cause of Grievance - the root cause as understood by the employee
  • Status - set as the grievance progresses (Draft, Submitted to HR, Approved by HR, Rejected By HR)

Approval & Notifications

Submitting a grievance ("Submit to HR" action) emails the Head of Corporate Services, who reviews and approves or rejects it. The workflow states are still labeled "Submitted to HR" / "Approved by HR" for historical reasons, but HR is no longer the recipient - the Head of Corporate Services owns the review.

Confidentiality

Grievance records are visible to the Head of Corporate Services, System Manager, and the employee who raised it. Details are not shared without consent except as required by the resolution process. Note this form is not anonymous - the reporter's identity (Raised By) is a mandatory, visible field.

What Happens Next

  1. The Head of Corporate Services reviews the submission.
  2. They investigate and engage the relevant parties.
  3. A resolution is proposed and documented in Resolution Details.
  4. The grievance status is updated to Approved or Rejected with reasons, and the employee is notified by email.

content:
Anonymous Employee Grievance

Purpose

A fully anonymous channel for reporting workplace concerns. Unlike the standard Grievance form, no name, employee ID, or contact details are ever captured. Reports go to the Head of Corporate Services only.

How to Submit

There are two ways to file an anonymous grievance:

  • Public Guest Form - visit /report-grievance from any browser, no login required. This is the only channel with no trace back to any ERP account.
  • Employee Desk - logged-in employees with the Employee Self Service role can use New > Anonymous Employee Grievance from the desk. The form itself asks for no identifying details, but Frappe's own account metadata (who was logged in when the record was created) is still technically recorded - use the Public Guest Form instead if that matters to you.

Form Fields

  • Grievance Type - category of the grievance
  • Severity - Low / Medium / High / Critical
  • Date of Occurrence
  • Description - required, full description of the issue
  • Cause of Grievance
  • Grievance Against Party / Grievance Against - who or what the complaint concerns (optional)
  • Witnesses - free text, optional

Tracking Code

On submission you receive a tracking code - a random, unguessable code that is the only way to check on your report afterwards. There is no password reset or account recovery: if you lose the code, the report cannot be retrieved or linked back to you by anyone, including the Head of Corporate Services. Write it down somewhere safe before leaving the page.

Staff note: desk records are also labeled with a readable reference like AEG-2026-07-0001 for internal use. That reference is separate from the reporter's tracking code and does not grant access to the status/reply pages - only the tracking code shown to the reporter does.

Checking Status & Replying

Visit /grievance-status and enter your tracking code to:

  • See the current status (New, Under Investigation, Resolved, Dismissed)
  • Read any messages left by the Head of Corporate Services
  • Send a reply

Because no contact details are stored, the Head of Corporate Services cannot email you - you must return to this page with your tracking code to see replies. There is no notification sent to you when a new reply arrives.

Who Can See It

Only the Head of Corporate Services and System Manager roles can view submitted reports on the desk. Employee Self Service users who filed via the desk channel can see only their own submission.

What Happens Next

  1. The Head of Corporate Services is notified by email that a new anonymous grievance was filed (no identifying details are included).
  2. They move the record to Under Investigation and may leave messages via the Correspondence thread.
  3. Check /grievance-status periodically with your tracking code to see replies and respond.
  4. The record is marked Resolved or Dismissed once the investigation concludes.

ERPNext is an open-source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that brings all of an organisation's core business functions into one platform. Instead of using separate tools for HR, finance, project tracking, and procurement, ERPNext connects them so that data flows seamlessly across departments.

At ICL, ERPNext is the central system for managing:

  • Project Management - project tracking, task assignments, work plans, and lessons learned
  • Procurement and Assets - requisitions, asset tracking, and custodianship
  • Finance - accounting, payroll, and expense reconciliation

Project Module

Purpose

The Project module is the central record for everything an engagement needs - team, timeline, budget, work plans, meetings, status reports and lessons learned. This guide walks through creating a project, adding the people who work on it, and where to manage the project day to day.


Project Lifecycle at a Glance

Every engagement moves through the same five phases, from kickoff to closeout. The sidebar under Project Management is grouped to match:

  1. Initiation - create the Project and its charter (this guide); see also HIS Project Quick Guide for HIS engagements.

  2. Planning - build the High Level Work Plan, Detailed Work Plan, Project Implementation Plan and Project Risk Assessment.

  3. Execution - run Project Meetings, sync tasks via Jira Integration, and track Project Deliverables & Payment Schedule and Project Manager Billing.

  4. Monitoring & Control - submit periodic Project Progress Reports, backed by Project Notifications & Automation.

  5. Closure - capture a Lessons Learned report (see its workflow and notifications guide) before the project is marked Completed.

Configuration shared across all phases - the Project Manager roster and notification contacts - lives in Project Management Settings; the standard document library lives in Project Toolkit Document Templates.

Key Concepts

  • Project - the master record. Most other documents (Timesheets, Travel Requests, Work Plans, Tasks, Meetings) link back to it.

  • Project Users - the team members granted access, each with an allocated level of effort (LOE).

  • Project Manager(s) - the employee(s) accountable for the project.

  • Project Phase - the project's current lifecycle stage: Initiation, Planning, Execution, Monitoring & Control, Post-Implementation Closeout or Closed.

  • ICL Project Management - the dashboard for working with a single project across tabs (Overview, Tasks, Team, Timesheets, Documents, Work Plan).

1. Create a Project

Go to New → Project (or the Projects list → Add Project) and fill the core details:


  • Project Name - a clear, unique title.

  • Status - Open, Completed or Cancelled.

  • Customer - the client the work is delivered for.

  • Department, Company and Priority.

  • Expected Start / End Date - the planned timeline.

Save to create the project.

2. Fill Project Information

Use the Project Information and related sections to record context:

  • Organisation, Role and Preferred Communication Method.

  • Donor and Partner Organisations - funding and collaborating bodies.

  • Project Opportunity Bid - link the originating Opportunity if the project came from a bid.

  • Jira Project - link the matching Jira project so issues can sync into Tasks (see the Jira Integration guide).

3. Add Project Users

Open the Users table on the project and add a row per team member:

  1. Select the User - their full name fills in automatically.

  2. Set Allocated LOEs - the level of effort (in days) committed to this project.

  3. Leave Welcome Email ticked if you want the user notified that they were added.

Project users gain access to the project and appear under the Team tab of the dashboard, with their allocated LOEs and total logged hours.

4. Assign Project Manager(s)

In the Project Manager tab, add the accountable employee(s) to the Project Manager(s) table. Each row links an Employee (with department), and project managers receive the project notifications and approvals.

5. Reporting & Notifications

  • Project Report Frequency - how often status reports are expected (e.g. Weekly, Monthly).

  • Allow Notification - enable to send project alerts to the team and managers.

6. Manage the Project in ICL Project Management

Open the ICL Project Management page and select the project to work in the dashboard. Tabs available:


  • Overview - meta, progress, financial snapshot and assignment.

  • Tasks - project tasks with search, pagination, and Pull from Jira when a Jira project is linked.

  • Team - project users with allocated LOEs and hours.

  • Timesheets - timesheets logged against the project.

  • Documents - File Manager and Google Drive folders.

  • Work Plan - High Level and Detailed Work Plans.

  • Lessons Learned - capturing what worked and what to improve.

  • Jira Integration - syncing Jira issues into project Tasks.

  • Project Implementation Plan - breaking planning down into tracked activities.

Key Concepts

  • Opportunity - the master bid record. Holds the client/party, opportunity amount, sales stage, and links to the Lead or Customer it came from.

  • Bid Status - where the bid currently stands: In-progress, Submitted, Pending, Review, Awarded, Not Awarded, Awaiting Feedback or Withdrawn.

  • Go/No Go - the internal decision on whether to pursue the opportunity, driven through the Opportunity Workflow (see below). A No Go always requires a written Reason for NO/GO, shown as a red banner at the top of the record so anyone opening it sees the decision immediately.

  • Opportunity Owners - the table of employees responsible for the bid; the most recently added Active owner is notified by email and becomes the acting owner.

  • Opportunity Checklist tab - where the working documents for the bid live: the system/Drive folders, the task checklist, technical and financial proposal files, and the Bid Development Templates table (see its own guide).

1. Create an Opportunity

Go to New -> Opportunity and capture the basics:

  • Opportunity From and Party - the Lead or Customer the bid is for.

  • Opportunity Type and Source.

  • Expected Closing, Sales Stage and Probability.

  • Bid Status and Go/No Go.

Save to create the record - this also creates a system folder for the opportunity's files if Create System Folder was ticked.

2. Go/No Go Workflow

The Opportunity Workflow routes the Go/No-Go decision for approval, then tracks the bid through to its final outcome:

  1. Draft - the Employee clicks GO or NO/GO, which sets Go/No Go to match and submits the opportunity to the CEO. Clicking NO/GO requires entering a Reason for NO/GO first.

  2. Submitted to CEO - the CEO reviews the employee's recommendation (emailed to them automatically) and makes the final call with the same GO / NO/GO actions, moving the record to Approved by CEO or Rejected by CEO.

  3. Approved by CEO - once the bid is actually submitted and a result comes back from the client, the Employee closes it out with Awarded (sets Bid Status to Awarded) or Lost (opens ERPNext's standard Set as Lost dialog to record lost reasons and competitors).

The workflow state is shown at the top of the form and drives who can act on the record next.

3. Finance, Risk & More Info

Before a bid is approved, these tabs capture the supporting review:

  • Finance tab - Currency and Opportunity Amount, the Budget Template (internal costed budget or an attached client template - see the Opportunity Budget Template guide), and a Finance Significance Review note.

  • Risk tab - Risk Level and Contextual Description and Risk Mitigation Strategies.

  • More Info tab - Implementation Capacity, Response Capacity, Submission Requirements, Operational Readiness to Execute, Technical Justification and general Notes.

  • Resources tab - free-text Client Resources notes.

4. Work the Opportunity Checklist

Open the Opportunity Checklist tab to manage the bid's working files:

  • Create System Folder / Create Drive Folder - provision a private Frappe file folder and/or a Google Drive folder for this opportunity's documents.

  • Task Checklist - the linked Opportunity Task Checklist tracking bid preparation tasks. Create one from the Create button at the top of the form if it isn't linked yet.

  • Bid Development Templates - select which standard bid templates apply to this opportunity and push them into its Google Drive folder. See the dedicated Bid Development Templates guide for the full workflow.

5. Manage Owners and Contributors

Use the Opportunity Owners table to assign who is accountable for the bid, and Contributors to add anyone else supporting it. Newly added active owners receive an automatic notification email.

Related Guides

  • Bid Development Templates - the standard template library and how to sync it to an opportunity's Google Drive folder.

  • Opportunity Budget Template - the costed budget (salaries, travel, indirect costs, Grand Total) behind the bid.

  • Project Module - once a bid is won, the resulting engagement is tracked as a Project, linked back to this Opportunity via Project Opportunity Bid.

Bid Development Templates

Purpose

The Bid Development Templates list is the shared library of standard bid documents - technical proposal outlines, financial proposal formats, compliance forms and other recurring bid paperwork. Maintain a template once here and reuse it on every opportunity, instead of tracking down the latest copy for each new bid.

Where to Find It

Search Bid Development Templates in the Awesomebar, or go to New -> Bid Development Templates to add one.

Key Fields

  • Document Name - a clear, unique label for the template (e.g. "Technical Proposal Outline"). This also becomes the record's ID.

  • Attach - upload the actual template file (Word, Excel, PDF, etc.).

  • Description - a short note on what the template is for and when to use it.

  • Is Active - tick once the template is ready to use. Only active templates appear when loading templates onto an Opportunity.

How to Add or Update a Template

  1. Open New -> Bid Development Templates (or the existing record if replacing a file).

  2. Set the Document Name and Description.

  3. Attach the file under Attach.

  4. Tick Is Active and save.

To roll out a newer version, replace the file under Attach on the same record and save - opportunities that later sync templates will pick up the new file.

Using Templates on an Opportunity

On an Opportunity's Opportunity Checklist tab:

  1. Click Load Bid Development Templates to pull in every active template as a row in the Bid Development Templates table. Untick Include in Drive Folder on any row you don't need for this bid.

  2. Click Create Drive Folder to create (or find, if one already exists with that name) a Google Drive folder for the opportunity - this also uploads every selected template into it in the same step.

  3. If a Drive folder for this opportunity already exists (e.g. created outside the system), click Attach Existing Drive Folder and paste its link instead of creating a new one. You can also paste the link directly into the Google Drive Folder field.

  4. Use Upload Templates to Drive at any time afterwards to push newly selected templates into the already-linked folder, without recreating it.

The Google Drive Folder field always shows the link currently attached to the opportunity, whether it was created by the app or attached manually.

Related Guides

  • Business Development Module - the full Opportunity lifecycle this fits into.

Opportunity Budget Template

Purpose

The Opportunity Budget Template is the costed budget behind a bid - salaries, fringe benefits, travel, other direct costs and indirect costs, rolled up into a Grand Total. It is built from a shared set of reusable budget line items, so every bid follows the same cost structure and totals are calculated automatically instead of by hand in a spreadsheet.

Key Concepts

  • Opportunity Budget Template - the actual budget record for one Opportunity (or Project). Has a Detailed Budget tab (line-by-line costs) and a Summary Budget tab (rolled-up totals by category), plus Grand Total fields. It is submittable, and is named automatically (OBT-YYYY-#####).

  • Payment Entry Budget Line - the master list of budget line items that defines the template structure (which lines exist, their order, section, and how their cost is calculated). Lines with Usage Context = Opportunity Detail Line populate the Detailed Budget tab; lines with Usage Context = Opportunity Summary Line populate the Summary Budget tab. Only Is Active lines are pulled in.

  • Row Type (on each detail line) - Manual (you enter Quantity and Rate, or a flat Cost), Formula (cost is a Percentage of one or more other lines, set via Formula Base), or Total (auto-sums every Manual/Formula line in the same Section).

  • Budget Against - whether this budget belongs to an Opportunity or a Project.

Internal Template vs Client Template

On the Opportunity form, the Budget Template section offers two sources, set via Budget Template Source:

  • Internal - link an Opportunity Budget Template record (create one from here, or link an existing one). This is the built-in, auto-calculating budget builder described below.

  • Client - the client has supplied their own budget format. Attach it directly under Client Template instead of building one internally.

Creating or linking an Internal template automatically sets Budget Template Source = Internal and writes the link back onto the Opportunity - no need to set it manually.

Building an Internal Budget

  1. Open New -> Opportunity Budget Template (or create it from the linked Opportunity). Set Budget Against = Opportunity and pick the Opportunity, and set the Currency.

  2. Open the Detailed Budget tab. Every active template line is added automatically. For each Manual row, enter a Quantity and Rate (or type a Cost directly) - Unit and Budget Narrative are free text for context.

  3. Formula and Total rows calculate themselves - Formula rows as a Percentage of their Formula Base lines, Total rows as the sum of their Section. Recalculation happens automatically as you edit quantities, rates and percentages.

  4. Check the Summary Budget tab and the Totals section - Total Other Direct Costs, Total Programs Expenses, Indirect Costs on All Costs and Grand Total - to confirm the bid's final cost.

  5. Save (and submit, once the budget is final).

Changing the Template Structure

To add, reorder, or change how a budget line is calculated across every Opportunity Budget Template, edit the master Payment Entry Budget Line list (System Manager) - set its Usage Context, Section, Row Type, Line Order and, for Formula lines, Default Percentage and Formula Base. New or changed active lines are picked up the next time a budget template is opened - existing budgets are not retroactively rewritten, only re-synced on save.

Related Guides

  • Business Development Module - the full Opportunity lifecycle this fits into.

  • Bid Development Templates - the document (Word/Excel/PDF) template library, separate from the costed budget covered here.

Asset Registration (Fixed Assets)

Purpose

Asset Registration is how physical assets - laptops, phones, office chairs, monitors, routers, and similar equipment - are entered into ERPNext as Asset records. Once registered, an asset can be tracked by custodian, location, and value, and is available for depreciation, movement, repair, and eventual disposal.

Key Concepts

  • Item - the master record describing a type of thing your organisation buys, stocks, or uses, e.g. "Dell Latitude Laptop" or "Office Chair". An Item is a template - it does not by itself represent one physical, trackable unit.

  • Asset - a single, individually tracked physical unit of an Item, e.g. the specific laptop with serial number XYZ issued to one developer. Each Asset record has its own value, location, custodian, and depreciation - so 5 identical laptops purchased together become 5 separate Asset records, all pointing back to the same Item.

  • Is Fixed Asset (checkbox on Item) - tells ERPNext "this Item represents something we own and use long-term, not something we resell or consume", e.g. laptops and chairs vs. stationery or raw materials. Ticking it is what makes the Item selectable when creating an Asset record - without it, ERPNext treats the Item as ordinary stock/consumable, and no Asset can be created for it.

  • Asset Category - groups similar assets (e.g. IT Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures) and holds shared defaults - which accounts to post value/depreciation to, and the default depreciation method and useful life - so you don't set those individually on every asset.

  • Custodian - the employee currently responsible/accountable for the asset. Changes over time as assets are reassigned; recorded via Asset Movement.

  • Location - where the asset physically is (an office, floor, or site), separate from who is using it.

  • Depreciation - the gradual reduction of an asset's book value over its useful life (e.g. a laptop bought for 100,000 might depreciate to 0 over 3 years). Applies to assets that lose value over time through use, like electronics; low-value or long-lasting items like basic furniture are often registered without depreciation, per company policy.

  • Existing Asset - an asset your organisation already owns and is only now recording in the system, as opposed to a brand-new purchase going through Purchase Receipt/Invoice.

Before You Start: One-Time Setup

These masters only need to be created once per organisation, then reused for every asset.

  1. Asset Category - go to Asset Category list and create one category per type of asset, e.g. IT Equipment (laptops, phones, monitors), Furniture & Fixtures (chairs, desks), Office Equipment (printers, routers). Each category can set default depreciation method, useful life, and accounts.

  2. Asset Item - go to Item and create one Item per asset type (e.g. "Dell Latitude Laptop", "Ergonomic Office Chair", "iPhone 14"). Tick Is Fixed Asset and set the Asset Category - this is what makes the item registrable as an Asset.

  3. Location - go to Location and create entries for where assets are kept or used, e.g. "Head Office", "Nairobi - Dev Floor".

  4. Company Fixed Asset Accounts - confirm the Company has Fixed Asset, Accumulated Depreciation, and Depreciation Expense accounts set (Accounts settings), so asset value posts correctly.

Registering a New Asset

  1. Go to Assets workspace and open the Asset list. Click New.

  2. Select the Item Code (the fixed-asset Item created above) - Asset Name and Asset Category pull in automatically.

  3. Set Company and Location.

  4. Set Custodian - the employee responsible for the asset - and Department.

  5. Set Purchase Date and Available For Use Date (when depreciation, if any, starts).

  6. Enter Gross Purchase Amount. If this asset was purchased through a Purchase Receipt or Purchase Invoice, link it instead of entering the amount manually so the value stays consistent with accounting.

  7. If registering assets you already own (not a new purchase), tick Is Existing Asset so no new purchase transaction is expected.

  8. If the asset should depreciate (typical for laptops and phones, less common for basic furniture), tick Calculate Depreciation and set Depreciation Method, Total Number of Depreciations, and Frequency - the depreciation schedule generates automatically.

  9. Save, then Submit. A submitted Asset is officially registered and ready for use/tracking.

Example: Registering a Developer's Laptop

  1. Item Code: Dell Latitude Laptop (Asset Category: IT Equipment).

  2. Company: your company - Location: "Nairobi - Dev Floor" - Custodian: the developer it is issued to.

  3. Purchase Date and Available For Use Date: date issued.

  4. Gross Purchase Amount: the purchase cost (or linked Purchase Invoice).

  5. Calculate Depreciation ticked, e.g. Straight Line, 3 years useful life.

  6. Save and Submit. Repeat with the matching Item (e.g. "Office Chair", "iPhone 14") for chairs and phones - furniture typically has Calculate Depreciation left unticked if it is treated as a low-value, non-depreciating asset per company policy.

Registering Many Assets at Once

For a large batch of identical or near-identical assets (e.g. 20 new laptops in one purchase):

  • Create the Purchase Receipt/Invoice with the fixed-asset Item and the required quantity - ERPNext can auto-create one Asset record per unit.

  • Alternatively, use the Data Import tool against the Asset doctype with a prepared spreadsheet for existing assets that were not purchased through the system.

After Registration

  • Asset Movement - record when an asset changes location or custodian.

  • Asset Repair - log repairs/maintenance against the asset.

  • Asset Custodianship Requisition - use this in-app process when formally assigning/handing over a registered asset to an employee.

Common Errors

  • Item not selectable as Asset - the Item is missing Is Fixed Asset or an Asset Category.

  • Missing Fixed Asset account error on submit - the Company's Fixed Asset/Depreciation accounts are not configured; set them in Company/Asset Category before submitting.

  • Wrong depreciation start - check Available For Use Date, not Purchase Date, since depreciation runs from that date.
